drivingQuestion: Is the mishna's ruling that she returns what she took superfluous?
outcomeNote: the clause is needed to rule out keeping seized property

segments.he: נָטְלָה מִזֶּה וּמִזֶּה. פְּשִׁיטָא! מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: כֵּיוָן דְּתָפְשָׂה לָא מַפְּקִינַן מִינַּהּ, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.
segments.en: § The mishna also teaches that if «she took» any of the above «from this» man «or from that» one she must return anything she took. The Gemara comments: This «is obvious.» Since she is not entitled to these articles, of course she must give them back. The Gemara explains: It is necessary, «lest you say» that «since she has» already «taken hold» of them «we do not remove» them «from her» possession, as this is merely a penalty and she obtained nothing that did not legally belong to her. The tanna therefore «teaches us» that the court requires her to return even these items.
